guide.headline: Weigman and Houston's front owned this one
guide.hook: A five-star senior quarterback ran into an overmatched UCF line, and Houston's passing-downs machine did the rest.

items.title: Weigman adds touchdowns with his legs
items.what: Conner Weigman threw for 239 yards on 18 of 33 with zero touchdowns and zero picks, but he ran 13 times for 50 yards and three touchdowns. For a quarterback with 11 passing touchdowns and an 8.8 yards per attempt average on the season, finding his scores on the ground tells you Houston adjusted mid-game. Watch his footwork resetting after the first read is covered, that's the trait that got him to 92 on this radar.
items.when: Every called quarterback run near the goal line

items.title: Houston's front lived in the backfield
items.what: Houston ranks No. 15 of 138 at the line of scrimmage with a 2.32 mark, while UCF's offensive line sits at No. 93 with just 2.96 line yards per carry. That 57 percentile point gap is not a lean, it's a mismatch, and it shows up as negative runs before UCF backs even get moving. Watch tackles for loss in the first quarter, that's where this game got decided up front.
items.when: First quarter, every early-down run by UCF

items.title: Houston never got stopped on third and long
items.what: Houston ranks No. 2 of 138 on passing downs at 51% success, while UCF ranks No. 45 on defense at just 25%. On third-and-medium specifically Houston throws it 53% of the time and converts 65%, the No. 4 rate in the country, against a UCF defense that allows 53% there. Two third-and-long conversions in a half was enough to break UCF's plan, and Houston had the volume to get them.
items.when: Third and medium to long, especially in the first half

guide.cardLine: Houston's front dominated UCF's line while Weigman ran in three scores, a complete mismatch on both sides of the ball.
